options.name: Manual script-driven workflow
options.description: Manual execution of analysis, preparation, training, validation, and deployment transitions, suitable for infrequently changing models.

options.name: Orchestrated ML pipeline
options.description: Connected, repeatable pipeline stages for preparation, feature extraction, training, tuning, evaluation, and deployment.

options.name: Standalone managed cloud ML platform
options.description: Runs model development, training, and deployment on a managed cloud ML service without an explicitly combined pipeline-platform or pluggable-engine strategy.

options.name: Managed pipeline-centered infrastructure
options.description: Uses managed ML pipeline components as the primary workflow infrastructure, potentially alongside a managed cloud ML platform for execution and deployment.

options.name: Hybrid multi-engine workflow infrastructure
options.description: Combines managed ML services and pipeline capabilities with pluggable execution engines so workflows can run across selectable or specialized runtimes.

options.name: Separated training and inference workflow
options.description: Coordinates training separately from prediction serving in the ML workflow.

options.name: Offline training pipeline
options.description: Executes model training as an offline workflow rather than as an online training process.

options.name: Instrumented execution wrapper
options.description: Uses an execution wrapper to inject context, record artifacts, and mediate runtime concerns around practitioner code.

options.name: Jupyter-centered interactive workflow
options.description: Uses interactive notebooks, particularly Jupyter, as the primary environment for exploratory analysis and sustained ML development.

options.name: Jupyter-and-IDE development workflow
options.description: Combines interactive notebook work with a general-purpose data-science IDE for more sustained or structured programming.

options.name: Cloud-hosted integrated notebook-and-IDE workflow
options.description: Uses a managed cloud notebook environment together with interactive notebook work, sustained notebook editing, and IDE-style development capabilities.

options.name: Containerized notebook execution
options.description: Notebook workflows are executed inside containers, without requiring a particular cell-ordering discipline or separate build process.

options.name: Containerized chronological notebook execution
options.description: Notebook workflows are containerized and depend on cells executing in chronological order to preserve computational state and narrative dependencies.

options.name: Containerized chronological execution with a notebook-independent build process
options.description: Notebook workflows are containerized and chronologically stateful, while a separate build process or continuous-integration quality gate is used alongside the notebooks.

options.name: Object-oriented production code organization
options.description: Organizing ML implementation as maintainable object-oriented programs rather than primarily interactive cells.

options.name: Deployable and understandable model code
options.description: Generated modeling code is kept understandable, maintainable, and ready for production deployment.

options.name: Collaborative reusable asset development
options.description: Develops data-science assets collaboratively to improve reuse, maintainability, and continuity.

options.name: Disconnected script-based asset organization
options.description: Organizes data-science assets as disconnected scripts across languages, locations, or environments.

options.name: Ad hoc asset documentation
options.description: Documents data-science assets informally without a standardized documentation approach.

options.name: Poor-quality data-science code
options.description: Uses code quality insufficient for reliable reuse, maintenance, and asset value.

options.name: Complex mixed technology stack
options.description: Uses a heterogeneous and complex technology stack that makes data-science assets difficult to reuse.

options.name: Explicitly specified production dependencies
options.description: Production packages, images, and runtime resources are declared so execution environments can be provisioned and reproduced. Development or notebook environments are not necessarily governed by the same dependency policy.

options.name: Explicit production dependencies with unpinned development environments
options.description: Production dependencies are declared, while notebook or model-development environments may rely on library versions that are not explicitly pinned across machines.

options.name: Centralized dependency-injected cross-cutting services
options.description: Shared functionality spanning ML layers or pipelines is organized centrally and supplied to components through dependency injection rather than being independently implemented or configured in each component.

options.name: Architectural technology guidance
options.description: Enterprise ML technology selection follows architectural guidance rather than unconstrained individual tool preference.

options.name: Unrestricted exploratory technology choice
options.description: Exploratory work allows broad choice of programming languages, tools, and frameworks.

options.name: Expertise-led enterprise technology selection
options.description: Enterprise technology is selected primarily by individual practitioner familiarity rather than architectural guidance.

options.name: Non-functional technology evaluation
options.description: Technology choices are assessed for staffing, expertise cost, maintenance, and other non-functional concerns.

options.name: Ad hoc distributed script implementation
options.description: Scripts distributed across languages, tools, machines, and servers are rejected as an enterprise delivery approach.

options.name: Low-code AutoML toolkit
options.description: Model development is exposed through a low-code toolkit for practitioners without Python expertise.

options.name: Boxed ML or AutoML solution
options.description: Uses a prepackaged ML or AutoML product rather than custom, tailored workflow components.

options.name: Automated ML lifecycle workflows
options.description: Automates recurring infrastructure, pipeline, deployment, and operational activities across the ML lifecycle without prescribing a particular tool composition or organizational scope.

options.name: Composable DataOps-centered ML toolchain
options.description: Composes specialized, replaceable services into an automated ML pipeline whose lifecycle management is centered on data operations rather than full model-lifecycle operations.

options.name: Configurable integrated MLOps and IT-operations platform
options.description: Provides a configurable, largely out-of-the-box platform that integrates lifecycle automation, MLOps practices, toolchain components, investment scaling, DataOps, and ML-driven IT operations.

options.name: Production engineering and DevOps omission
options.description: Leaving production engineering and DevOps practices out of a notebook-centered ML workflow.

options.name: Interchangeable AIOps and MLOps use
options.description: Treats AIOps and MLOps as interchangeable lifecycle and operations approaches.

options.name: In-house MLOps infrastructure
options.description: Infrastructure owned and operated internally for MLOps.

options.name: Dedicated internal ML operations team
options.description: A dedicated in-house operations team manages production models and infrastructure.

options.name: Hybrid ML infrastructure operation
options.description: Operates ML workloads across both organization-managed and cloud infrastructure.

options.name: Self-managed ML platform
options.description: Builds and operates an organization-owned platform rather than purchasing a managed one.

options.name: Lean iterative ML development
options.description: Delivering ML capabilities through short, iterative development cycles and staged learning.

options.name: Siloed ML and application teams
options.description: Data science and application development responsibilities are separated into specialist organizational groups.

options.name: Analyst-led end-to-end model pipeline
options.description: Analysts can preprocess data, build pipelines, and produce trained models with limited specialist intervention.

options.name: Standardized ML process model
options.description: Adopts a defined process model with templates and implementation guidance for predictive analytics work.

options.name: Cultural change for ML adoption
options.description: Treats organizational cultural change as a prerequisite for adopting agile ML and enterprise transformation methods.

options.name: Waterfall or V-model process
options.description: Uses heavyweight sequential development processes for analytics and software delivery.

options.name: Cross-functional ML delivery team
options.description: Combines software engineers with data scientists or ML researchers for exploration, development, and production delivery.

options.name: External specialist engagement
options.description: Uses a consultant or external specialist for initial data work and implementation support.

options.name: Staged scoped delivery
options.description: Scope the ML problem and deliver it through proof-of-concept and MVP stages before treating it as a production solution. This alternative emphasizes incremental validation of both technical feasibility and stakeholder value.

options.name: Production-validated delivery
options.description: Frame the ML problem around demonstrated value in real production use, using operational adoption and outcomes—not only sandbox or pilot performance—as the validation threshold.

options.name: Unified release automation
options.description: Models and their surrounding services are built, tested, packaged, and released through one automated process.

options.name: Commit-triggered staged release automation
options.description: Repository changes trigger automated builds, tests, artifact promotion, and deployment across delivery stages.

options.name: Environment-gated deployment automation
options.description: Deployment automation varies by environment, with progressively stronger validation and approval gates before production.

options.name: Recovery-oriented release automation with manual intervention
options.description: The release process supports automated deployment and restoration of prior versions, while allowing manual debugging or deployment during service recovery.

options.name: Progressive release automation with rollback
options.description: Production updates are introduced incrementally and can be reverted to a previous version when the release causes problems.

options.name: Artifact version control
options.description: ML artifacts and their dependencies are versioned as managed assets, providing a baseline for reproducible deployment and reuse.

options.name: Pipeline and experiment version control
options.description: Pipeline definitions, ML artifacts, and experiments are versioned together so alternative configurations and training results can be compared and reproduced.

options.name: Comprehensive ML lifecycle traceability
options.description: Pipeline designs, artifacts, experiments, training runs, metadata, deployment health, and datasets are governed through an integrated traceability approach.

options.name: Data-to-model lineage management
options.description: Dataset versions and profiles are linked to reproducible training context, model metadata, registry information, and deployment status.

options.name: Pipeline-based CI/CD governance
options.description: Pipeline designs, experiments, lifecycle metadata, registered models, and deployment health are managed through an operational CI/CD governance process.

options.name: End-to-end reproducible lifecycle governance
options.description: A standardized governance approach covers pipeline design, artifact dependencies, experiments, training snapshots, metadata, model health, and dataset versions across the complete ML lifecycle.

options.name: ETL-based feature ingestion
options.description: Batch extraction, transformation, and loading of row-level features from external data sources.

options.name: Streaming feature ingestion
options.description: Continuous or event-driven ingestion of base features from external sources.

options.name: Dual-path event and data ingestion
options.description: Routing interaction inputs simultaneously through low-latency event processing and durable dense-data processing.

options.name: Messaging-based data ingestion
options.description: Ingesting source data through message queues, middleware, or publish-subscribe channels.

options.name: Change-data-capture ingestion
options.description: Ingesting source-system changes through change-data-capture mechanisms.

options.name: Push-based data delivery
options.description: Having source systems push data into databases or pipelines.

options.name: Event-stream data sourcing
options.description: Uses operational event streams as the source for ML data rather than raw database or lake dumps.

options.name: Raw-dump data sourcing
options.description: Sources ML data directly from database dumps or data-lake schemas.

options.name: Query-based data extraction
options.description: Pulling source data by querying and extracting it from other systems.

options.name: Denormalized or aggregated training dataset
options.description: A cleaned, denormalized, or aggregated feature dataset is materialized as training input.

options.name: Automated data preprocessing
options.description: Automates cleaning, imbalance handling, missing-value treatment, leakage control, and resource-aware preprocessing.

options.name: Automated feature engineering
options.description: Automatically generates and selects features within the ML data pipeline.

options.name: Feature lifecycle cleanup
options.description: Removes unused or deprecated features and records their removal from infrastructure.

options.name: Shared data-processing pipeline reuse
options.description: Reuses common ETL, data-quality, and feature-engineering pipelines across teams instead of duplicating them.

options.name: Traceable and preserved data
options.description: Data is ingested with provenance and retained in an immutable form so that its origin, processing history, and original state remain recoverable.

options.name: Cataloged data
options.description: Data is governed through a metadata catalog that records its structure, profile, versions, aliases, and operational characteristics.

options.name: Privacy- and policy-validated data
options.description: Data preparation protects sensitive information and automated checks verify that data and feature pipelines comply with applicable policies.

options.name: Access-controlled preserved data
options.description: Retained data is made available through controls that restrict use according to users, organizational scope, and compliance context.

options.name: Integrated end-to-end data governance
options.description: Data governance is implemented as an integrated lifecycle covering traceable ingestion, cataloging, preservation, privacy protection, and policy compliance.

options.name: Central analytical ML data platform
options.description: Prepared product data is transferred to a shared analytical data platform, where ML and data-engineering pipelines expose data for downstream use. The platform may combine analytical storage with ML-oriented preparation.

options.name: Online feature-serving pipeline
options.description: A shared preparation pipeline produces and materializes features in a low-latency serving store for online model inference.

options.name: Durable end-to-end feature platform
options.description: An end-to-end platform prepares data, serves features in real time, and persists engineered feature data for reuse in training, recovery, and subsequent inference.

options.name: Online/offline feature-store architecture
options.description: Features are maintained in complementary online and durable stores, separating low-latency inference access from persistent training and reuse needs.

options.name: Human-in-the-loop data labeling
options.description: Uses domain experts and controlled review workflows to create labels for ML datasets.

options.name: Active-learning sample selection
options.description: Programmatically selects uncertain or error-prone production inputs for labeling.

options.name: API-mediated dataset access
options.description: Training and evaluation services obtain their respective datasets through a dedicated segregation or access API.

options.name: Local consolidation of external data
options.description: Persisting externally served data with local records to avoid repeated runtime service queries.

options.name: External curated dataset sourcing
options.description: Using a named external repository or curated dataset as the training-data source.

options.name: Local sensitive-data storage
options.description: Keeping sensitive ML data on local machines rather than in protected server-side storage.

options.name: Data availability and throughput requirements
options.description: Setting source-data availability, processing-speed, and scalability requirements for ingestion and access.

options.name: Vertically scalable training
options.description: Training scales primarily by using a larger machine rather than distributing computation across machines.

options.name: Horizontal and vertical training scalability
options.description: Scales training by adding resources or increasing capacity of existing resources.

options.name: Distributed event computation
options.description: Executing high-volume event processing across distributed computation infrastructure.

options.name: Fault-tolerant partitioned training
options.description: Uses checkpoints, error tolerance, and failover to recover partitioned training after transient failures.

options.name: Parallel candidate training
options.description: Multiple algorithms, parameter combinations, or candidate models are trained concurrently for comparison.

options.name: Automated model-family selection
options.description: The solution automatically selects among learner families according to predictive performance, computational cost, or workflow objectives, without requiring a dedicated model-building service or ensemble.

options.name: Service-based configurable model building
options.description: A reusable model-building service trains and selects models through configurable algorithms, parameters, and metrics. It can support interchangeable learner implementations and specified families such as random forests.

options.name: Ensemble-oriented automated modeling
options.description: The solution combines multiple models, potentially using an automated or packaged AutoML process to select and blend them for improved predictive performance or stability.

options.name: Fixed learner-and-objective configuration
options.description: The solution uses a deliberately specified predictive learner together with a task-specific objective, such as gradient-boosted trees with a binary logistic objective.

options.name: Nonlinear online learner
options.description: A nonlinear learner is considered for online data but rejected when its adaptation speed is insufficient.

options.name: Linear online learner
options.description: Linear or logistic regression is used for efficient, explainable, parameter-only online prediction.

options.name: Feature-enhanced linear learner
options.description: Feature engineering, interaction terms, or hashing extend a linear learner's representation capacity.

options.name: Incremental online training
options.description: Models are updated incrementally as new data arrives, using optimization suited to online learning.

options.name: Automated hyperparameter optimization
options.description: Searches model configuration and training hyperparameters automatically.

options.name: Manual hyperparameter tuning
options.description: Uses hand-selected trial-and-error experiments to tune model hyperparameters.

options.name: Model optimization objective selection
options.description: Selects the performance objective or error type that automated model optimization should prioritize.

options.name: Client-side model training
options.description: Trains models on client devices rather than in a centralized server environment.

options.name: Federated model-update learning
options.description: Models learn through exchanging model updates rather than transferring personal training data to a central server.

options.name: Offline evaluation pipeline
options.description: Candidate models are evaluated against held-out data and true values before deployment selection.

options.name: Threshold-based quality regression testing
options.description: Quality thresholds detect gradual degradation across versions and sudden drops in a new model.

options.name: Previously-built-model diff testing
options.description: Direct diff-testing against previously built ML models is explicitly rejected because it is difficult to maintain.

options.name: Held-out test-set isolation
options.description: Keeps a sampled test set unseen during model selection to prevent data snooping.

options.name: Interpretability-oriented model evaluation
options.description: Evaluates or explains model behavior to support compliance and understanding of predictions.

options.name: Metric-driven candidate model evaluation
options.description: Evaluates multiple candidate models on validation data using a selected performance metric.

options.name: Risk-specific model evaluation
options.description: Evaluating models against the particular harms or attack categories relevant to the business.

options.name: Business-impact-aligned evaluation
options.description: Evaluating models by whether algorithmic metrics correlate with business outcomes and user impact.

options.name: Fairness and inclusion evaluation
options.description: Testing model performance for fairness, bias, inclusion, and protected-category effects.

options.name: Model staleness testing
options.description: Testing whether outdated data or business-impact performance makes a model stale.

options.name: Separated training and test-data collection
options.description: Keeping procedures and teams for training and test data collection methodologically independent.

options.name: Feature predictive-power evaluation
options.description: Tests whether candidate features improve predictive performance before inclusion.

options.name: Feature infrastructure cost evaluation
options.description: Compares feature latency, dependencies, and memory costs against predictive value.

options.name: Single-objective evaluation
options.description: Treats one aggregate error-minimization objective as the sole basis for model evaluation.

options.name: Automated full-pipeline integration testing
options.description: The complete data, code, training, and evaluation pipeline is repeatedly executed and validated.

options.name: Production canary validation
options.description: A model is loaded into production and checked on real-life data before wider serving.

options.name: Prediction API contract testing
options.description: Checks expected request and response contracts after model or service changes.

options.name: Prediction-service load and latency testing
options.description: Tests serving throughput and response latency under operational load.

options.name: Training health validation
options.description: Validates convergence and numerical health, including absence of NaN results.

options.name: Target-infrastructure compatibility testing
options.description: Checks package, memory, compute, and accelerator compatibility with the serving environment.

options.name: Feature and model unit testing
options.description: Tests feature-engineering logic and model methods for implementation defects.

options.name: Schema and domain validation testing
options.description: Validates data and feature schemas and domains across training and serving stages.

options.name: Automated data-and-model validation
options.description: Automatically validates training data and models before retraining or deployment.

options.name: Real-time prediction-quality monitoring
options.description: Prediction quality and model behavior are measured immediately or continuously after serving when labels are available.

options.name: Input and feature-drift monitoring
options.description: Feature-generation processes, schemas, statistical values, and unusual inputs are monitored for changes.

options.name: Threshold-based retraining
options.description: Quality degradation or data-value shifts trigger retraining, while schema anomalies halt execution for investigation.

options.name: Passive production operation
options.description: The system does not actively track predictions or model performance after deployment.

options.name: Automated retraining pipeline
options.description: Automatically retrains models using new production or labeled data.

options.name: Schedule-based retraining trigger
options.description: Starts retraining on recurring daily, weekly, or monthly schedules.

options.name: Data-availability retraining trigger
options.description: Starts retraining when newly collected training data becomes available.

options.name: Performance- or drift-based retraining trigger
options.description: Starts retraining after model degradation or feature-distribution drift is detected.

options.name: Business-impact monitoring
options.description: Monitors decision quality, business goals, risks, fairness, segments, and use-case-specific error costs.

options.name: Software-metrics-only monitoring
options.description: Limits monitoring to generic software metrics without ML quality or impact measures.

options.name: Downstream-KPI-only monitoring
options.description: Relies exclusively on delayed downstream business KPIs to detect model problems.

options.name: Automated failure recovery
options.description: Automatically recovering deployed ML operations from failures with minimal intervention.

options.name: Human oversight of deployed models
options.description: Combines automated predictions with human intervention and review during production operation.

options.name: Manual retraining trigger
options.description: Relies on a practitioner to restart model training when retraining is needed.

options.name: Rule-based fraud detection
options.description: Detects fraud using short-window metric anomalies and recurring behavioral heuristics.

options.name: Production logging and security observability
options.description: Operates production ML with logging, security controls, monitoring, and observability.

options.name: Model-decay planning
options.description: Plans operational processes for performance decay caused by changing data and production conditions.

options.name: Periodic model health checks
options.description: Reviews deployed models at recurring intervals instead of continuously monitoring them.

options.name: User-reported model issue detection
options.description: Uses user reports as the mechanism for discovering production model problems.

options.name: Custom model-monitoring dashboard
options.description: Builds an internally tailored dashboard with model-specific checks and operational views.

options.name: Ad hoc model-insight analysis
options.description: Investigates model behavior through custom scripts and manual analysis when deeper insight is requested.

options.name: Separate model and business-KPI monitoring
options.description: Maintains model-monitoring interfaces separately from business KPI reporting tools.

options.name: Service-health and data-quality monitoring
options.description: Monitors latency, memory, uptime, data quality, dependencies, and data shifts alongside model performance.

options.name: Root-cause performance diagnosis
options.description: Uses monitoring to quantify changes and diagnose causes of production performance problems.

options.name: Stateless horizontally scaled serving
options.description: Serving instances avoid durable serving state and handle requests independently, scaling out by adding replicas.

options.name: Asynchronous message-driven serving
options.description: Production components communicate through non-blocking messages and queues, decoupling request handling from downstream work.

options.name: Horizontally scaled Redis-backed asynchronous serving
options.description: Stateless or independently scalable serving instances use Redis for feature or queue storage while exchanging work asynchronously.

options.name: Geographically redundant asynchronous serving
options.description: Serving is distributed across regions or continents, using asynchronous operation and failover to maintain availability under regional failures.

options.name: Atomic distributed stateful serving
options.description: Scalable serving maintains model, feature, or auxiliary state in memory and Redis, updates shared parameters atomically, and distributes work asynchronously.

options.name: Compute-optimized training hardware
options.description: Training uses hardware optimized for high single-threaded computational performance rather than memory capacity.

options.name: Scale-to-zero serving
options.description: Reduces serving capacity to zero when demand falls to control operating cost.

options.name: CPU-or-GPU resource allocation
options.description: Selects CPU or GPU capacity as a service for cluster job execution.

options.name: Replicated mutable model instances
options.description: Replicating model instances behind load balancing for serving or learning workloads.

options.name: Full-dataset in-memory retention
options.description: Keeping the complete training dataset in memory during model updates.

options.name: Elastic resource scaling
options.description: Compute resources scale automatically with ML workload demand.

options.name: Large-scale data processing capacity
options.description: Runtime infrastructure is selected to handle very large ML data volumes.

options.name: Service resource and latency profiling
options.description: Profiles deployed services to measure resource use and response latency before sizing or placement.

options.name: ONNX inference optimization
options.description: Converts models to ONNX as a runtime optimization intended to improve inference performance.

options.name: REST prediction microservice
options.description: A model is exposed through an API-backed prediction microservice for application integration.

options.name: PMML-based model serving
options.description: PMML provides a portable model representation that supports compatible tooling and both online and distributed batch scoring.

options.name: Multi-source model input interface
options.description: An algorithm or serving interface that accepts trained models, processed data, and fresh live signals as distinct inputs.

options.name: Parallelized service data access
options.description: Obtaining independent service data concurrently rather than serially when assembling model-serving inputs.

options.name: Cross-service identifier translation
options.description: Mapping application identifiers to external service identifiers before retrieving model-serving data.

options.name: Adoption of external service identifiers
options.description: Using a third-party service's identifier as the application's primary lookup key.

options.name: gRPC model interface
options.description: Exposing an independently deployed model through a gRPC interface.

options.name: Socket-based model interface
options.description: Using socket communication as the client-server interface for model-serving requests.

options.name: Containerized offline prediction service
options.description: A containerized service loads a model for on-demand or scheduled batch prediction.

options.name: Monolithic application architecture
options.description: The model is integrated within a single monolithic application structure.

options.name: Model-as-a-service deployment
options.description: Exposes predictions as a real-time model service integrated with product applications.

options.name: On-device edge inference
options.description: Runs model inference in deployed edge modules on hardware devices.

options.name: Amalgamated standalone model package
options.description: Packages model logic and runtime code into one portable deployable artifact.

options.name: Cross-format model serialization
options.description: Uses interoperable representations such as PFA, ONNX, or generated code for model serving.

options.name: Repository selection by workload
options.description: Selecting among storage repositories according to access patterns, consistency, latency, and workload needs.

options.name: Microservice integration architecture
options.description: Integrating ML capabilities through independently organized services rather than one application unit.

options.name: Hybrid microservice-monolith architecture
options.description: Combining independently separated services with shared components in one application architecture.

options.name: Long-running serving daemon
options.description: Keeping the model-serving server alive for the application's lifetime with maintenance interruptions.

options.name: Plug-in model architecture
options.description: Deployment architecture allows new recommendation or model approaches to be integrated as replaceable components.

options.name: Automatic container image generation
options.description: Creates the deployment container image automatically as part of model deployment.

options.name: Manually specified deployment image
options.description: Requires practitioners to specify the production container image used for deployment.

options.name: Strict microservice deployment architecture
options.description: Uses a strict microservice-oriented architecture for ML project deployment.

options.name: Client-side prediction placement
options.description: Places prediction execution on client devices rather than on a server.

options.name: Local deployment troubleshooting
options.description: Deploys a model locally to diagnose and debug production deployment problems.

options.name: Client-server prediction architecture
options.description: Places prediction requests and execution across client and server components.

options.name: Model-as-dependency deployment
options.description: The model is packaged and deployed with the consuming application for build-time and runtime availability.

options.name: Containerized inference deployment
options.description: Packages inference code and dependencies in a container for deployment across managed, on-premise, or hybrid runtimes.

options.name: Serverless zip-package deployment
options.description: Places serverless application code and dependencies in a zip artifact with a single entry point.

options.name: Direct deployment of offline-trained model
options.description: Deploys an offline-trained model directly as a prediction service without the required production conversion workflow.

options.name: Traditional Hadoop production architecture
options.description: Using a Hadoop-based architecture for production ML and fraud-processing workloads.

options.name: Container-orchestrated ML runtime
options.description: Runs containerized ML workloads under an orchestrator such as Kubernetes or a managed serverless container service.

options.name: Layered ML pipeline architecture
options.description: Separates data, computation, and serving-orchestration layers in the ML execution workflow.

options.name: Queue-fronted online serving cluster
options.description: Containerized online predictors are distributed across servers behind a queue for load balancing, throughput, and low latency.

options.name: Serverless function deployment
options.description: ML workloads are packaged as functions and executed through a serverless runtime with automated scaling and operational handling.

options.name: Scheduled batch prediction deployment
options.description: Deploys scheduled batch scoring and writes results to storage or analytics systems.

options.name: Report-based result delivery
options.description: Delivers predictions through dashboards, webhooks, SMS, or email reports.

options.name: Online computation serving
options.description: Computing predictions from current context and recent data during an online request.

options.name: Precomputed offline serving
options.description: Producing predictions in advance through periodic or batch computation for later serving.

options.name: Precomputed-result fallback
options.description: Serving an existing precomputed result when online computation cannot satisfy availability or latency requirements.

options.name: Offline-online serving parity
options.description: Keeping model behavior consistent between offline and online prediction contexts.

options.name: Hybrid offline-online serving
options.description: Combining precomputed results with online processing to add freshness at request time.

options.name: Production prediction persistence
options.description: Persisting production inputs and predictions for later monitoring, analysis, or evaluation.

options.name: Candidate-user assignment
options.description: Selecting users for shadow, canary, or A/B model exposure using lists, attributes, geography, or randomization.

options.name: Prediction-serving fallback behavior
options.description: Returning fallback results when online feature retrieval or inputs are unavailable or anomalous.

options.name: Threshold-based prediction decision
options.description: A prediction score is converted into an operational action through a configured threshold.

options.name: Neural architecture search
options.description: Automatically searches candidate neural-network architectures rather than selecting one manually.

options.name: Random architecture search
options.description: Samples candidate neural architectures randomly during architecture search.

options.name: Gradient-based architecture search
options.description: Uses a continuous relaxation and gradients to search neural-network architectures.

options.name: Evolutionary architecture search
options.description: Evaluates architectures and propagates successful child architectures while pruning unsuccessful ones.

options.name: Ecological-cost-aware architecture search
options.description: Optimizes architecture search with explicit attention to its ecological or carbon cost.

options.name: Multivariable fraud prediction model
options.description: Uses a machine-learning model combining multiple variables to identify fraudulent behavior.

options.name: Architecture search-space definition
options.description: Defines which neural-network architectures are eligible for automated architecture search.

options.name: Architecture evaluation metric selection
options.description: Selects the metric used to judge candidate neural-network architectures during search.
